data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/sh

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --job-name="perf_cylinder"
#   --partition=thin
#   --time=2-00:00:00
#   -n ${NP}
#   -o stdout-benchmark/slurm-%j-%4t-%n.out
#   -e stdout-benchmark/slurm-%j-%4t-%n.err

# NOTE: Slurm -n ${NP} depends on an environment variable NP at submission time.
# In this script, the launched MPI size is also taken from the first positional argument ($1).
# We preserve runtime behavior by using $1 as the task count for the allocation.

flux alloc \
  -n ${1} \
  --time=48h \
  --queue=thin \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: Slurm output/error patterns use Slurm-specific substitutions (%j, %t, %n) and width formatting (%4t).
# Flux does not provide a portable equivalent in the batch script.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but per-task/per-node log separation may be lost, which can make
# debugging performance issues (e.g., rank imbalance, noisy neighbors) harder.

# Best-effort: capture combined stdout/stderr to a single file using Flux job id.
exec >"stdout-benchmark/flux-${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>&1

source ../compile/modules_snellius.sh
export CASE_ID=1
echo "Starting case: $CASE_ID"

mpiexecjl --project=../ -n $1 julia -J ../PerforatedCylinder_parallel.so -O3 --check-bounds=no -e '\''include("run_case_benchmark.jl")'\''
'
"
}
